method: per impression: mean(feature | clicked) - mean(feature | not clicked), NaN values ignored; impressions without both classes skipped. Effect size dz = mean/sd of the differences (approx. 95% CI). Primary test: one-sample t-test of the differences against 0, Holm within each family. User-level check: each user's mean difference, one-sample t-test across users, Holm; significant_user also requires the same sign as dz. significant_both = both levels.
why_not_wilcoxon: Wilcoxon signed-rank assumes differences symmetric around 0 under the null. With 1-2 clicks against ~35 non-clicks and right-skewed features, the null distribution is asymmetric: with labels shuffled within impressions, Wilcoxon flagged 93/101 features (t-test: 0). Wilcoxon p, its Holm p and the rank-biserial are kept as robustness columns only.

robustness_columns.null_*: same analysis with labels shuffled within impressions (seed 42)

families.emotion_signal_variants_fit.csv: rows 'all candidates' are taken from the main family; 'candidates with abstract' is its own family (57)

limitations: no popularity control here: emotional tone may correlate with general item popularity; this is controlled later by the LightGBM M4 vs M5 pair
features are correlated, so Holm is conservative
with ~10^5 impressions tiny effects reach significance: read dz, not p
